title: Fake news, ads and AI fakes

slides.title: Three kinds of false
slides.text: Some false posts want different things. A scam wants your tap, a hoax wants your belief, and rage-bait wants your reaction and your share.
slides.alt: A post from Netville News Flash, “School to close forever!”, with clues marked: free candy for a year, and share before they delete this.

focus.cue: And it begs for your share

slides.title: Ads wear costumes too
slides.text: Not every friendly post is a friend talking. Sponsored posts are paid ads in a costume, and a glowing plug may be paid for too. Ask who benefits if you tap or buy.
slides.alt: A post from Prize Ad, “You won a phone!”, with clues marked: your free phone, and only the first fifty people.

focus.cue: An ad dressed up as a prize

slides.title: Check the source, not the pixels
slides.text: Edited and AI-made pictures can look perfect now, because fakes are cheap to make. So do not judge by the pixels. Judge by the source: who posted it, and can anyone else confirm it?
slides.alt: A post from Video Clip, “The mayor sings in a fountain!”, with a clue marked: his mouth moves after the words end.

focus.cue: The clue is in the details

slides.title: Stop before you share
slides.text: Use three moves on anything shocking: Stop. Find another source. Decide before sharing. A post you do not pass on cannot use you to travel.
slides.alt: The post's clues marked, then the debrief: real news does not beg to be shared before deletion. Check big stories with a trusted adult.

focus.cue: Stop: real news does not beg to be shared

slides.title: The Magpie's fake photo
slides.text: This morning the Magpie slipped a fake photo into Netville's post: Pim, it claimed, was closing the post office early. Here is how a Defender checked it.
steps: Stop: do not share it yet
Find another source: the real notice board
No other source backs it up
Decide: do not share; tell Pim
slides.alt: The clue marked, his mouth moves after the words end, then the debrief: some videos are made by computers to look real, AI fakes.

focus.cue: Show Pim, and check a real news page

words.means: a false story made to be believed and passed on
paid for, so a post or plug is really an ad
where a claim or picture really came from
to check a claim against another trusted source

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Trick Inbox at Fake or Fact? and sort all 6 posts. Run the three moves on each one: stop, find another source, then decide.
slides.alt: A post from Netville News, “New reading room”: the library opens its new reading room on Saturday.

focus.cue: Play Fake or Fact?: stop, check, then decide
